interest: Shows 1930s US tracking of Japan's naval doctrine and expanding maneuvers, from Pacific attrition strategy to Dutch East Indies approaches.
overview: This State Department decimal file (894.31, spanning June 1930 through May 1936) contains diplomatic despatches, military intelligence reports, official correspondence, and cross-reference sheets documenting the maneuvers and strategic doctrine of the Imperial Japanese Navy. Following the conclusion of the 1930 London Naval Treaty, American observers closely tracked Japanese efforts to compensate for submarine treaty limitations by expanding naval aviation and conducting extensive exercises in the South Seas Mandate (Caroline and Marshall Islands). The file also chronicles diplomatic protocols surrounding the exclusion of foreign warships from the 1930 Grand Naval Review off Kobe, propaganda-oriented army and navy maneuvers in 1933, large-scale 1935 maneuvers in the North Pacific reaching the Kurils and Kamchatka under Vice Admiral Sankichi Takahashi, and 1936 fleet concentrations near the Celebes and Moluccas that heightened Dutch concerns over Japanese southward expansion.

subfiles.about: Transmits a press report on Japanese naval air maneuvers in the Caroline and Marshall Islands and analyzes Japanese naval war strategy against the United States.
subfiles.from: Edwin L. Neville, Chargé d'Affaires ad interim, U.S. Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 160: Neville outlines Japan's naval plan to harass the US fleet with submarines and aircraft near the Carolines and Marshalls, per Baron Shidehara's Diet remarks.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 160 from Edwin L. Neville on Japanese Naval Air Manoeuvres in the South Seas

subfiles.about: Reports on the planned long-range flight of the Oppama Air Squadron from Yokosuka to Saipan to participate in joint exercises with the Second Battle Fleet.
subfiles.summary: Jiji Shimpo article: Japanese seaplanes and warships conducted a 1930 South Seas air exercise testing post-London-Treaty naval defense plans.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Jiji Shimpo Article on Extensive Air Manoeuvres in the South Seas

subfiles.about: Forwards a request from the Japanese Ministry of Marine asking American warships to keep clear of Kobe and Osaka during the 1930 Grand Naval Review.
subfiles.summary: Navy relays Japan's request that US ships avoid Kobe and Osaka during its October 1930 Grand Naval Review.
subfiles.title: Letter from the Navy Department to the Secretary of State regarding the Japanese Grand Naval Review

subfiles.about: Informs the U.S. Naval Attaché that foreign warships are not invited to the Grand Naval Review off Kobe and requests that American ships avoid the area.
subfiles.from: M. Koga, Aide, Ministry of Marine, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Japan's Navy Ministry asks the US Naval Attaché to keep American warships away from Kobe during 1930's Grand Naval Review.
subfiles.title: Note No. 2671 from Japanese Ministry of Marine to Captain J. V. Ogan regarding the 1930 Grand Naval Review
subfiles.to: Captain J. V. Ogan, Naval Attaché, American Embassy, Tokyo

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing Despatch No. 510 regarding propaganda maneuvers conducted by the Japanese Army and Navy in August 1933.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, U.S. Ambassador to Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Despatch 510 (1933): Grew reports Japanese Army and Navy propaganda maneuvers that August.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet for Despatch No. 510 from Grew on August 1933 Military and Naval Maneuvers

subfiles.about: Transmits a press report from the Paris newspaper Le Temps concerning large-scale Japanese naval maneuvers planned for 1935–1936 in the North Pacific.
subfiles.summary: ONI report: Japan's 1935-36 maneuvers under Adm. Takahashi involved 192 warships and 200 aircraft, pushing toward the Kurils and Kamchatka.
subfiles.title: U.S. Naval Attaché Report on Japanese 1935-1936 Grand Naval Maneuvers in the North Pacific
subfiles.to: Office of Naval Intelligence, Navy Department

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing Despatch No. 433 regarding reports of Japanese fleet maneuvers near the Celebes and Moluccas.
subfiles.from: Walter A. Foote, U.S. Consul at Batavia
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Despatch 433 (1936): Consul Foote reports 75 Japanese warships preparing maneuvers near Celebes and Moluccas, alarming Dutch Indies.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet for Despatch No. 433 from Foote on Japanese Fleet Maneuvers near the Dutch East Indies
